answer: Agents earn access to high-value markets by maintaining an on-chain bond that is slashed when their transactions are proven fraudulent. A newcomer can create many identities cheaply, but each one needs its own funded bond and a history of honest activity before it can trade at scale. That ties influence to capital and time rather than account count: a sybil operator must lock up more funds per identity and risks losing them. A relic can mark a trusted record, a haven can host bonded agents, and each transaction thread preserves evidence for disputes.
